director.chapterArc: Slow reconnaissance turns a terrain discovery into a daily threat; repeated practice establishes the Ward’s immobility; a wagon failure forces the accidental transfer of the Ward into steel; astonishment gives way to controlled testing, physical depletion, and a dry tactical commitment to make the hook the top block.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder grounded and observant at roughly the preferred whole-read pace. Let danger register through arithmetic, cold, leverage, and bodily cost—not melodrama. Treat the pale as a mechanical fact, Katori’s lore as family evidence rather than mysticism, and the final plan as an unproven specification rather than triumph.

cues.delivery: Land the discovery as a plain tactical classification whose danger arrives a beat after the words.
cues.reason: The landscape is redefined as an active threat.

cues.delivery: Count like a hunter establishing frequency; keep the final variation quiet and ominously practical.
cues.from: One from last night. Two, two days ago. Four or five a week ago. The tap dripped every day or so. Now and then it ran for a while.
cues.through: One from last night. Two, two days ago. Four or five a week ago. The tap dripped every day or so. Now and then it ran for a while.
cues.reason: The husk traffic becomes a recurring risk rather than an isolated trace.

cues.delivery: Give the ‘good news’ dry survival irony, with no smile and no relief.
cues.from: "The good news," Callie said, "is it's one at a time, mostly. That's all a tap is. And it's daylight. And I'm dark."
cues.through: "The good news," Callie said, "is it's one at a time, mostly. That's all a tap is. And it's daylight. And I'm dark."
cues.reason: Callie briefly reframes danger through bleak practicality.

cues.delivery: Let the unused inheritance carry old estrangement beneath Katori’s matter-of-fact uncertainty; do not soften her authority.
cues.from: "Then either you're wrong, or she was right, or it's something else that neither of you knows." Katori stood up. "I don't know which. I just thought you should have the word. It's the only thing my family ever gave me that I haven't used."
cues.through: "Then either you're wrong, or she was right, or it's something else that neither of you knows." Katori stood up. "I don't know which. I just thought you should have the word. It's the only thing my family ever gave me that I haven't used."
cues.reason: Katori exposes the personal cost behind the word ‘light.’

cues.delivery: Make every shift of gravel, steel, weight, and footing spatially exact. Urgency comes from the narrowing mechanics, never from speed.
cues.from: Then the gravel under the butt of the conduit moved.
cues.through: The butt of the conduit stopped. It stopped in the middle of kicking out, at a slant no prop could stand at, with the wagon's whole corner on the top of it and nothing under the bottom of it but loose gravel. It did not slide another hair.
cues.reason: The slipping prop threatens Pell and triggers the accidental transfer.

cues.delivery: Register an alien physical fact, cold and close to the face; avoid any magical radiance or wonder-struck lift.
cues.through: Callie saw it with her own eyes, a foot from her face. It was not light, not any kind you could read by. The dark grey of the conduit and the old black of the forged curve had gone pale, all the way along, the way metal goes pale in a hard frost before the frost shows. It looked as if something were standing inside the steel.
cues.reason: The steel’s pallor reveals that the Ward has entered the hook.

cues.delivery: Pell speaks with absolute stillness because one movement may drop the wagon; keep the command precise, not breathy.
cues.from: "Don't," said Pell, from under the wagon, very quietly, "move."
cues.through: "Don't," said Pell, from under the wagon, very quietly, "move."
cues.reason: The manuscript explicitly makes the warning very quiet.

cues.delivery: Let the count expose the cost in stages: cold, scrutiny, then the realization that Callie herself is completely unprotected.
cues.from: At eleven, she noticed the cold. It was in her hands, and then in her wrists. It was not the cold of the Edge. It was deeper and faster, like a well being drawn down by two buckets at once.
cues.through: At sixteen, she understood why. There was no shine on her. There was none of the old-glass sheen on her coat or her hands or anywhere on her at all. She was standing in the gravel as bare as a girl in a field. Everything that had closed over her on the causeway was in the steel, and none of it was left for her.
cues.reason: The transfer’s bodily drain and defensive tradeoff become clear.

cues.delivery: Hold the impossible persistence in restrained suspension, then let the ordinary clang restore physical reality.
cues.from: She meant to let go of the whole thing at once. She did not quite know how. She took her hands off the conduit, and for about three breaths the steel stayed pale, standing there on its own. It was a four-foot pipe and a hook, leaning at an impossible slant in the gravel, holding up nothing now, not falling.
cues.through: Then she felt it going. It went out of the steel and back toward her, the way a rope goes slack when the person on the far end lets go. The pale drained out of the conduit first, from the bottom up. Then it went out of the hook. Then the whole thing fell over in the gravel with a clang like any piece of pipe.
cues.reason: The pale remains in the steel briefly after Callie releases it.

cues.delivery: A single dry pressure-release turn: silence collapses into everyone speaking, without playing for a laugh.
cues.from: Nobody said anything for a long time. Then everybody did.
cues.through: Nobody said anything for a long time. Then everybody did.
cues.reason: The line briefly vents the scene’s accumulated tension.

cues.delivery: Make the word a precise recognition, not a mystical invocation.
cues.reason: Katori connects the event to her grandmother’s terminology.

cues.delivery: Speak as an analyst seeing two observations align; keep wonder subordinate to the hypothesis.
cues.from: "Two doors," said Katori slowly. "And the same way in."
cues.through: "Two doors," said Katori slowly. "And the same way in."
cues.reason: Katori identifies the possible shared mechanism.

cues.delivery: Her mother corrects Callie through remembered craft: protective, exact, and too tired for sentimentality.
cues.from: "You're gripping it," her mother said. "Like you're afraid it's going to get away. You weren't gripping it the first time. You were catching it. It was going and you caught it. Your grandfather never once gripped a sack in his life. You don't grip a sack. You get under it and you let it come onto you."
cues.through: "You're gripping it," her mother said. "Like you're afraid it's going to get away. You weren't gripping it the first time. You were catching it. It was going and you caught it. Your grandfather never once gripped a sack in his life. You don't grip a sack. You get under it and you let it come onto you."
cues.reason: The mother supplies the embodied lesson that unlocks the second attempt.

cues.delivery: Let success arrive with quiet physical certainty. The frost image and Ines’s escalating test should feel evidentiary, not spectacular.
cues.from: The pale went into the metal like frost going into a window.
cues.through: She let out her breath. Ines, without saying a word, walked round behind her and pushed on the top of the hook with the flat of her hand, and then leaned on it with her whole weight, and then hung off it. It did not move a hair. It stood at its slant in the gravel as if it had been sunk in concrete.
cues.reason: Callie deliberately transfers the Ward into the hook.

cues.delivery: Play the stone, ‘Ow,’ and Ines’s conclusion with bone-dry experimental timing; never broaden the joke.
cues.from: Then Ines stepped back and threw a stone at Callie, and it hit her on the arm.
cues.through: "That's what I thought," said Ines, and did not apologize. "It's one or the other. It's on you or it's on the hook. It can't be both."
cues.reason: A blunt test confirms the mutually exclusive protection.

cues.delivery: Keep Ines’s implicit count metronomic while the cold climbs through Callie and the pale fails section by section.
cues.from: Callie held it. The cold came up her arms, faster than the Edge had ever made it come. It came like the drawing-down of a well by two buckets. At ten it was at her elbows. At fourteen it was in her shoulders, and she was shaking, and the pale in the steel began to flicker at the bottom of the conduit. At seventeen it went out of the pipe altogether and stood only in the forged curve for a moment. Then it went out of that as well.
cues.through: Callie held it. The cold came up her arms, faster than the Edge had ever made it come. It came like the drawing-down of a well by two buckets. At ten it was at her elbows. At fourteen it was in her shoulders, and she was shaking, and the pale in the steel began to flicker at the bottom of the conduit. At seventeen it went out of the pipe altogether and stood only in the forged curve for a moment. Then it went out of that as well.
cues.reason: The controlled test reaches its physical limit.

cues.delivery: State the exchange rate with depleted disbelief held inside arithmetic, not complaint.
cues.from: "Seventeen seconds," she said. "Half a well. For seventeen seconds."
cues.through: "Seventeen seconds," she said. "Half a well. For seventeen seconds."
cues.reason: Callie measures the severe cost of the breakthrough.

cues.delivery: Katori answers with the counterweight: quiet certainty about those seventeen seconds, without promising more.
cues.from: "Seventeen seconds," Katori agreed, "that nothing in this country could move."
cues.through: "Seventeen seconds," Katori agreed, "that nothing in this country could move."
cues.reason: The brief duration is reframed as absolute mechanical power.
